issue: The derivation note that the figure caption explicitly points to ('Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below') prints a formula that is arithmetically wrong as written: 'L* = N/(n_layers-d) = 70 x (80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens'. The printed expression evaluates to 45,875,200, not 106.8K, and the operator is multiplication where division is required. The correct expression is N* = N_params/(n_layers x d) = 70e9/(80 x 8,192) = 106,811 ~ 106.8K (and 53.4K for the full-square convention, N_params/(2 x n_layers x d)). The two crossover values printed in the figure are correct; the formula that produces them is not.
evidence: Printed 340: 'L* = N/(n_layers-d) = 70 x (80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens'. Recomputation: 70 x 80 x 8,192 = 45,875,200 (not 106.8K). Correct: 70e9 / (80 x 8,192) = 70e9 / 655,360 = 106,811.5 = 106.8K; full-square: 70e9 / (2 x 655,360) = 53,405.8 = 53.4K. Both printed crossover values are reproduced exactly by the corrected formula, confirming the intended derivation.
acceptance_test: Print the derivation as N* = N_params/(n_layers x d) = 70e9/(80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens (full-square: N_params/(2 x n_layers x d) = 53.4K), with N_params defined as 70e9 and the units of N* stated as tokens. A reader must be able to reproduce 53.4K and 106.8K by substituting the printed symbols, with no implicit 10^9 and no inverted operator.

figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), left-panel magenta annotation
issue: The in-figure annotation 'full-square quad overestimates ~53.4x' attaches the number 53.4 to the word 'overestimates', which is a category error and invites a false inference: the reader will conclude that the full-square convention overstates the true attention cost by a factor of 53.4. 53.4K is a crossover CONTEXT LENGTH, not an overestimate factor. The book's own note states the actual overstatement factor is exactly 2x (halving the attention term for the causal mask doubles the crossing).

Printed 340: 'Causal-triangle: halving the attention-part term (see (iii) - a causal mask) doubles the crossing ... so the ~53.4K figure is a property of the full-square convention, and the causal kernel moves it to ~106.8K.' The overstatement factor is 2x; 53.4K is a length on the x-axis.
acceptance_test: Replace the annotation with a statement that names the quantity and the axis, e.g. 'full-square: quadratic = linear at ~53.4K tokens' (and, if the 2x overstatement is worth keeping, state it separately as 'full-square counts 2x the causal attention work'). issue: The caption's takeaway contradicts the derivation note printed on the facing page and the figure's own crossover annotations. The caption says the quadratic attention term 'overestimates the parameterized-linear term at ~53.4K context tokens under full-square counting and ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting, so at 128K it is large but not yet dominant.' By the book's own arithmetic, at 128K the quadratic term is ~2.4x the linear term (full-square) and ~1.2x the linear term (causal-triangle), i.e. it is already the LARGER of the two terms and is 54-71% of total prefill FLOPs. 'Not yet dominant' is false under both conventions and directly contradicts the note on the same spread.
evidence: Printed 340: 'at 128K it is ~2.4x the linear term (linear + quadratic, i.e. 1.2x), and total prefill FLOPs at 128K are ~3.4x the 2N_L baseline'. Independent check: ratio = (N/N*)^2 with N* = 106.8K (causal) gives (128/106.8)^2 = 1.44; with N* = 53.4K (full-square) gives (128/53.4)^2 = 5.74. Either way the quadratic term exceeds the linear term at 128K, so the caption's conclusion is wrong.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the takeaway so it states the crossover as an equality point ('the quadratic term equals the parameterized-linear term at ~53.4K under full-square counting and ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting, and exceeds it beyond those lengths') and replace 'not yet dominant' with the book's own computed ratios at 128K (2.4x full-square / 1.2x causal-triangle, i.e. the quadratic term is already the larger term). Verify the revised sentence against Note 22.1-1 so the caption and note state the same numbers.
